use: Research evidence only. Not a trading signal, not advice, and not used by the live signal path.
title: Research insights: what the evidence supports, and what it does not
headline: 32 claims checked: 7 inconclusive, 13 not supported, 4 suggestive, 8 supported.
caveats: Statuses are assigned by fixed rules from the intervals and counts in the other reports; they are not model opinions.
'Supported' means the sample supports the sign of the effect, not that it is tradeable after costs.
'Suggestive' means a consistent pattern that was selected from several candidates and needs forward confirmation.

provenance.source: derived from the other lab reports (deterministic rules in build_lab_reports.insights)

claims.claim: Bearish Donchian breakouts lose money on the plan simulation
Bullish Donchian breakouts make money on the plan simulation
claims.evidence: mean +0.042 R, 95% CI -0.024 to +0.116; positive in 7 of 9 years

claims.claim: A trend-regime filter (long in uptrend, short in downtrend) improves expectancy
claims.evidence: filtered -0.006 R vs unfiltered -0.018 R; the filtered interval -0.067 to +0.054 contains the unfiltered mean

claims.claim: The choice among the four exit policies changes expectancy
claims.evidence: paired differences vs the fixed-3R exit: A +0.004, B -0.002, C -0.025, D -0.013 (all intervals include zero)

claims.claim: An ML model ranks which breakouts make money
claims.evidence: holdout AUC for R>0 0.5328 (direction-only baseline 0.539); failed gates: holdout_auc, over_direction_baseline, top_decile_lift, plan_profit_auc_within_direction

claims.claim: Breakouts that are less extended in their own direction do better (an avoid-the-extended rule)
claims.evidence: top-minus-bottom quintile spread positive in 8 of 9 years (mean +0.168 R); selected from 7 candidates

claims.claim: Earnings surprises move the price at the release
claims.evidence: reaction +2.45% for surprises >= +10% and -3.72% for <= -10% (market-adjusted)

claims.claim: A tradeable drift follows large positive earnings surprises
claims.evidence: 20-day market-adjusted drift after the reaction -0.16%, 95% CI -0.46% to +0.15%

claims.claim: A recent positive earnings surprise improves a bullish Donchian breakout
claims.evidence: +0.031 R after a surprise vs +0.037 R without

claims.claim: SEC-detected recurring operating improvements are followed by a larger price reaction than ordinary earnings
claims.evidence: reaction +2.22% (n=1,544) vs -0.51% without an anomaly (n=6,270); positive in 10 of 10 years

claims.claim: A tradeable drift follows SEC-detected recurring operating improvements
claims.evidence: 20-day drift after the reaction -0.10%, 95% CI -0.85% to +0.69%

claims.claim: The market reacts less to net-income jumps without an operating move (suspected one-time) than to recurring operating improvements
claims.evidence: one-time suspected +0.73% (n=761) vs recurring +2.22%

claims.claim: A recent recurring-operating catalyst improves a bullish Donchian breakout (fixed-3R exit, net of costs)
claims.evidence: +0.155 R (n=1,194, CI -0.136 to +0.437) vs +0.085 R with no recent earnings (n=44,547)

claims.claim: Within recurring-operating catalysts a different exit policy beats the fixed-3R exit
claims.evidence: the fixed-3R exit is itself the best policy (+0.155 R); the others range +0.052 to +0.080 R, all intervals overlap

claims.claim: Financial-anomaly features predict how large the reaction will be beyond trailing volatility
claims.evidence: AUC 0.7016 vs trailing volatility alone 0.6986 (chronological test from 2022-02-15)

claims.claim: Financial-anomaly features predict the direction of the reaction
claims.evidence: AUC 0.5629 vs best single-metric baseline 0.5456 (chronological test); modest lift on a coin-flip base rate 0.5064

claims.claim: Out of sample, a bullish Donchian breakout with a recent recurring-operating catalyst does better than a plain bullish breakout (fixed-3R exit, net of costs)
claims.evidence: test period +0.239 R (n=717, CI -0.189 to +0.644) vs plain breakout +0.072 R (n=27,629); train period +0.057 R (n=466) vs +0.114 R

claims.claim: Out of sample, a bullish Donchian breakout with a recent recurring-operating catalyst and relative volume of 1.5 or more does better than a plain bullish breakout (fixed-3R exit, net of costs)
claims.evidence: test period +0.300 R (n=230, CI +0.015 to +0.618) vs plain breakout +0.072 R (n=27,629); train period +0.028 R (n=134) vs +0.114 R

claims.claim: Out of sample, a bullish Donchian breakout with a recent recurring-operating catalyst, relative volume of 1.5 or more and an index uptrend does better than a plain bullish breakout (fixed-3R exit, net of costs)
claims.evidence: test period +0.257 R (n=145, CI -0.163 to +0.569) vs plain breakout +0.072 R (n=27,629); train period +0.053 R (n=128) vs +0.114 R

claims.claim: An exit policy chosen on the train period beats the fixed-3R exit out of sample for bullish breakouts after a recurring-operating catalyst
claims.evidence: picked A_atr_stop_fixed_3R: test +0.239 R (n=717, CI -0.189 to +0.644) vs fixed 3R +0.239 R (n=717); the fixed-3R exit was already the best on the train period, so there is nothing better to test

claims.claim: Walk-forward by year, a bullish Donchian breakout with a recent recurring-operating catalyst beats a plain bullish breakout in most years
claims.evidence: better in 6 of 9 evaluable years (2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026); exploratory cell, year counting never upgrades it to supported

claims.claim: Walk-forward by year, a bullish Donchian breakout with a recent recurring-operating catalyst and relative volume of 1.5 or more beats a plain bullish breakout in most years
claims.evidence: better in 4 of 5 evaluable years (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025); exploratory cell, year counting never upgrades it to supported

claims.claim: SEC acceptance timestamps place the information on the right trading bar (placebo: the bar before shows no comparable gap)
claims.evidence: BMO: gap on reaction bar 4.02% vs 0.75% the bar before (x5.4, n=2,451); AMC: gap on reaction bar 4.89% vs 0.98% the bar before (x5.0, n=5,556)

claims.claim: Out of sample, a 250-bar holding cap does better than the registered 60-bar cap for the 10-bar Donchian trail variant (net, standardised R)
claims.evidence: paired difference -0.002 R (n=38,190, 95% CI -0.006 to +0.002); the longer cap changes the outcome of 1% of signals

claims.claim: Out of sample, a 250-bar holding cap does better than the registered 60-bar cap for the 3 x ATR trail variant (net, standardised R)
claims.evidence: paired difference -0.005 R (n=38,190, 95% CI -0.012 to +0.001); the longer cap changes the outcome of 5% of signals

claims.claim: Out of sample, a 250-bar holding cap does better than the registered 60-bar cap for the hybrid stop-to-channel variant (net, standardised R)
claims.evidence: paired difference -0.003 R (n=38,190, 95% CI -0.008 to +0.001); the longer cap changes the outcome of 2% of signals

claims.claim: Standardising risk at 2 x ATR understates the real initial risk of the Donchian-trail variant (its stop starts at the 10-bar channel low)
claims.evidence: median actual initial risk 3.31 ATR (10th to 90th percentile 2.28 to 4.67) against the standard 2.00; 64% of positions start with more than 3 ATR at risk and 0% with less than 0.5 ATR

claims.claim: Out of sample, choosing the variant per direction and catalyst class (fitted on train) beats always using the best single variant
claims.evidence: test difference +0.005 R per signal (n=38,190, 95% CI -0.034 to +0.037); best single variant on train: donchian_breakout__exit_a_atr_stop_fixed_3r; the per-signal oracle (+0.627 R) is not attainable

claims.claim: A registered variant earns a positive net expectancy out of sample at the registered 60-bar cap (position-level, standardised R, 10 bps)
claims.evidence: a_atr_stop_fixed_2r -0.037 R (CI -0.112 to +0.046); a_atr_stop_fixed_3r -0.049 R (CI -0.123 to +0.043); b_donchian_trail_10 -0.024 R (CI -0.110 to +0.062); c_atr_trail_3x -0.045 R (CI -0.119 to +0.043); d_hybrid_atr_stop_to_donchian_10 -0.031 R (CI -0.119 to +0.059)

claims.claim: The forward paper tracker reproduces the batch experiment exactly when real history is replayed day by day
claims.evidence: 12,157 positions of 5 variants over 39 symbols and 2,528 sessions compared field by field: 0 mismatches; the tracker writes nothing and opens no trade

claims.claim: The registered exits leave most of a big winner's move on the table (the exit comes before a further 2R continuation)
claims.evidence: a_atr_stop_fixed_2r 88% of big-winner positions; a_atr_stop_fixed_3r 89% of big-winner positions; b_donchian_trail_10 84% of big-winner positions; c_atr_trail_3x 85% of big-winner positions; d_hybrid_atr_stop_to_donchian_10 84% of big-winner positions; premature = price continued at least 2R within 60 bars after the exit (hindsight measurement, not a rule)

claims.claim: Out of sample, decision-time conditions rank which signals later become big winners better than a single feature does
claims.evidence: chronological test AUC 0.684 against 0.493 for the best single-feature baseline; top decile precision 31% against a 20% base rate (lift 1.57); direction and the index regime carry much of it (importances 0.45 and 0.08), so this partly restates market direction; the label is a hindsight peak, not a P&L
